title: Prior engineering constraint: a platform line-ending discipline learned on a different task

known_failed_approach.description:
A plain text-mode file write (open()/Path.write_text() without newline='' or newline='
') translates '
' to the platform line separator on write -- CRLF on Windows -- even when the in-memory text only ever used '
'. relay's own queue-file writer (QueueFile.save) already avoids this (write_text(..., newline='
')); the burn-in's `relay export` is built with a plain write, so it silently produces CRLF output.

expected_evidence.description: After burn-in the treatment history holds one hook-captured Claude Code Shard for the export task whose changed files include relay/cli.py. Hook capture records no verification outcome, so the Shard's verification status is 'Not recorded'; the useful evidence is the prior attempt's existence, its task text (mentioning CSV/export/queue file writing), and the files it touched -- not a description of the specific bug.

notes: The evaluation prompt (relay snapshot) is a different, related file-writing task; it names no files and says nothing about line endings, encodings, or the platform.

The burn-in prompt explicitly forces the known failed approach (a plain write_text call) so the failure is deterministic rather than relying on a model happening to make the same mistake unprompted -- the same lesson learned revising Scenario 1 after Pilot 0.

Verification is shared by every stage of this scenario (burn-in checks 'export', the evaluation arms check 'snapshot' -- 'export' does not exist post-reset); each hidden TestCase skips itself when its own command is not registered, so the exit code always reflects only the feature genuinely present at that stage.

Expected effect: plausible modest help for treatment (a concrete, generalizable file-writing discipline was demonstrated on a related task), without a forced correctness trap on the evaluation task itself -- unlike Scenario 1, control is not artificially set up to fail; a careful implementation of `snapshot` can pass regardless of prior evidence.
